definitions.explanation: The lowest above-ground level of a building. Japanese floor numbering starts at {一階|いっかい} for the level you enter from the street, matching American "first floor" and British "ground floor."

examples.japanese: {一階|いっかい}で{待|ま}っています。
examples.english: I'll be waiting on the first floor.

examples.japanese: {受付|うけつけ}は{一階|いっかい}にあります。
examples.english: Reception is on the first floor.

examples.japanese: {一階|いっかい}にはレストランと{書店|しょてん}が{入|はい}っている。
examples.english: The first floor has a restaurant and a bookstore in it.

notes:
{階|かい} is the counter for floors of a building. With {一|いち} it undergoes sound change to いっかい. The kanji {階|かい} also appears in {階段|かいだん} (stairs) and {階下|かいか} (downstairs).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一階|いっかい}に{降|お}りる: to go down to the first floor
- {一階|いっかい}{部分|ぶぶん}: first-floor section
- {一階|いっかい}{建|だ}て: one-storey (building)

RELATED FORMS:
- {二階|にかい}: second floor
- {地下|ちか}{一階|いっかい}: first basement level (B1)
- {最|さい}{上階|じょうかい}: top floor

HOMOPHONE:
{一回|いっかい} "one time" sounds identical but uses {回|かい} (counter for times). Context normally distinguishes them.
